This website documents the data, statistical analyses, and publication outputs
for a multi-country study of excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The repository contains the exact source snapshots used for the analysis and
separates computationally intensive model fitting from lightweight reporting.

## Manuscript figures and table

Each page provides the manuscript caption, the code used to construct the
publication artifact from precomputed analysis results, and downloadable output.

| Publication item | Description |
|:--|:--|
| [Figure 1](figure_01.html) | Seasonally Adaptive Mortality Model illustration |
| [Figure 2](figure_02.html) | Initial- and Delta-wave P-scores in Europe |
| [Figure 3](figure_03.html) | Initial- and Delta-wave P-scores in North America |
| [Figure 4](figure_04.html) | P-scores by vaccination group over time |
| [Figure 5](figure_05.html) | Female-minus-male P-score differences over time |
| [Table 1](table_01.html) | Wave-specific P-scores for selected regions |

## Regional analyses

The [regional analyses](regional_analyses.html) page maps the common estimands to
the source-specific pipelines for Europe, England and Wales, Ireland, Canada,
and the United States. The [statistical methods](methods.html) page records the
shared model and summary definitions.

## Supplementary analyses

The [supplementary overview](supplementary.html) provides a frozen inventory,
summary definitions, and complete downloads. Interactive pages expose
[geography-specific mortality and P-score time series](supplementary_timeseries.html)
and [all four wave-specific map summaries](supplementary_wave_maps.html) without
loading posterior draws or fitted model objects in the browser.

## Reproducibility

Exact reproduction uses the versioned files under `data/raw/`. Provider-hosted
data may subsequently be revised; the optional access scripts retrieve current
versions without replacing the repository snapshots. See [data sources](data_sources.html)
and [reproduction instructions](reproduction.html) for details.

Model fits and posterior draws are intentionally excluded from Git because they
are large and computationally expensive to recreate. Website generation reads
the tracked publication figures and table and does not refit any model.
